summary: The UAE golden visa is a long-term residence scheme (not citizenship), created by Cabinet Resolution 56/2018 (in force Feb 2019; AED 10 million or AED 5 million property) and rebuilt in 2022 (Res. 65/2022: 10-year permits from AED 2 million in property, deposit or company share, or AED 250,000 a year in taxes). There is no official statistical series: counts are press statements, mostly from Dubai GDRFA and covering all golden-visa categories (47,150 in 2021, 79,617 in 2022, about 158,000 in 2023, 66,000 in H1 2026), plus one Cabinet claim of 500,000 UAE-wide in 2024; no investor-only counts or investment totals are published beyond launch-time estimates (6,800 eligible, AED 100 billion). Since 2021 citizenship is possible only by nomination, with no price and no published numbers; the FATF grey listing (2022-2024) did not cite the golden visa.

Replaced by Cabinet Resolution No. 8 of 2021, which we could not find online; that resolution was in turn repealed by Cabinet Resolution No. 65 of 2022 (art. 79). events.description: Golden residence becomes 10 years for all categories, with wider family sponsorship and no limit on time abroad; real-estate investors qualify from AED 2 million including mortgaged and off-plan property. In force 90 days after publication.
events.location: paras "Golden Residence" and "Golden Residence for Real Estate Investors"
events.quote: Substantial amendments are introduced to the Golden Residence Scheme to simplify the eligibility criteria and expand the categories of beneficiaries.

events.title: Cabinet Resolution 65/2022 in force; golden residence rules moved to its annex
events.description: Executive regulation of Decree-Law 29/2021 takes effect; art. 77 puts golden residence under an annex and art. 79 repeals Cabinet Resolution No. 8 of 2021 on golden residence permits.

programs.name: UAE Golden Visa (الإقامة الذهبية - golden residence; long-term residence for investors, entrepreneurs and talents)
programs.notes: Long-term residence without a sponsor. Created by Cabinet Resolution 56/2018 (in force 3 Feb 2019; permits issued from 21 May 2019): investors AED 10 million (10 years) or AED 5 million in property (5 years). Replaced by Cabinet Resolution 8/2021 (text not found), then by the annex to Cabinet Resolution 65/2022 (in force 3 Oct 2022): 10-year permits, AED 2 million in property, bank deposit or company share, or AED 250,000 a year in taxes. Issued by ICP federally and by GDRFA in Dubai. Gives no path to citizenship: there is no residence period that leads to naturalisation; citizenship is only by nomination (see are-citizenship-nomination). Official counts are press figures covering all golden-visa categories, mostly Dubai only; no investor-only series is published.

programs.name: UAE citizenship by nomination for investors and talents (amended Executive Regulation of Federal Law No. 17 of 1972 on Nationality and Passports)
programs.notes: Not a citizenship-by-investment programme with a price: candidates (investors who own UAE property, doctors, scientists, inventors, artists, and their families) cannot apply; they are nominated by Rulers' and Crown Princes' courts, executive councils or the Cabinet. Dual nationality allowed; citizenship can be withdrawn if conditions are breached. No numbers of grants have been published. Announced by WAM on 30 Jan 2021; the amended regulation itself was not found.

new_indicators.name: Long-term ("golden") residence permits issued, all categories
new_indicators.definition: Long-term residence permits (e.g. UAE golden visas) issued in a period across all eligibility categories (investors, entrepreneurs, talents, professionals, students, and family members if the source includes them); not limited to investors, and not distinguishing first grants from renewals unless noted
new_indicators.notes: Use residence_permits_issued (with breakdown route=...) for investor-only counts. UAE figures are mostly Dubai (breakdown emirate=dubai).

new_indicators.name: People identified as eligible for an investor residence scheme
new_indicators.definition: Number of people the authorities say qualify for (or are targeted by) a residence-by-investment or long-term residence scheme at a date; not permits issued
new_indicators.notes: A target or eligibility pool, often announced at launch.

new_indicators.name: Existing investments of people identified as eligible
new_indicators.definition: Official estimate of the investments already held by the people identified as eligible for a residence scheme; not new investment attributable to the scheme

gaps: Annex to Cabinet Resolution 65/2022 (golden residence rules, uaelegislation.gov.ae/ar/legislations/1601/regulations/653/download): could not be saved or read (Cloudflare), so 2022 legal thresholds come from the Cabinet summary and emirate service pages, not the legal text.

Cabinet Resolution No. 8 of 2021 on golden residence permits (in force 2021 to 2 Oct 2022): text not found online; we do not know if it lowered the AED 5 million property threshold or the AED 10 million investment threshold before 2022, so valid_to/valid_from dates around 2021-2022 are uncertain.
No investor-only counts: no official figure split golden visas by category (investor, real estate, talent, student) after 2019; all counts cover every category.
No federal (ICP) annual series of golden visas issued; only the Cabinet claim of 500,000 for 2024 (reported by Al Khaleej), which may be cumulative or include renewals.
No figures for Abu Dhabi or the other emirates; no figures on renewals or revocations.
No official totals of investment brought in by golden-visa investors (only the 2019 estimate of existing investments of the 6,800 eligible, and AED 200 million for one 20-investor batch).
Dubai 2024 and 2025 annual golden-visa counts not found.
Citizenship by nomination: the amended executive regulation of Federal Law 17/1972 was not found, and no number of naturalisations of investors has ever been published.
FATF material does not tie the grey listing to the golden visa; FATF 2020 Mutual Evaluation of the UAE not read for any mention of residence by investment.
Most official PDFs could not be stored: uaelegislation.gov.ae and fatf-gafi.org block scripted downloads (Cloudflare); only Res. 56/2018 was saved.
